Fits reuse Pantheon, BOSS DR12 and other BAO families. Planck releases and SH0ES calibrations differ but inherit observations/calibrators. Fits are not independent confirmations; exact cross-analysis covariance remains unknown.
Timescape modifies averaging/observer-distance interpretation at late epochs; it is not an added pre-recombination fluid or EDE potential.
Historical TS comparisons depend on reduction and cuts; this limits cosmological interpretation without proving either model.

The early segment shares positive extra energy reducing a fixed-endpoint sound-horizon integral. The unified late phase and tracking history are not equivalent to the parent background mechanism over all epochs.

Here one smoothly rolling tracking scalar must retain a late-dark-energy role via slope features. Existing oscillating EDE depletes around a potential minimum; matching an early averaged EOS or ruler shift is not equality of potential, trajectory or perturbations.

The reviewed unified mechanism uses smooth scalar rolling; first-order phase conversion with a separate trigger is explicitly outside its obstruction. The restriction is not a critique excluding NEDE.
The variance identity excludes positive exponential sums as a realization of the required nonmonotonic slope ordering in this domain; it does not exclude the shoulder example.
The percent-scale baryon-free scaling residue motivates an independent depletion slope; Appendix sign and baryon limitations remain explicit.

A late Higgs-triggered parent-to-daughter conversion and daughter-only interaction is not single-scalar early/late tracking unification. Decays are an excluded extra process in the scalar obstruction; this paper does not thereby furnish a unified EDE scenario.

Both use transition language, but this converts late dark-matter species after symmetry breaking. It is not the established early false-vacuum energy release/bubble-percolation mechanism, and no equivalence of transitions or perturbations is accepted.
Challenges promotion of chosen background overlap to inherited full cosmological fits; does not reject the gauge-invariant decay operator itself.

The interacting vector is a separate proposed majority dark-matter component, whereas A/B form the decaying subcomponent. SIDM is an optional gauge extension, not evidence for the expansion mechanism.
q interpolation specifies kinematics without a scalar action, stress-energy or perturbation closure; matching a late q curve would not identify a unified scalar theory.
Finite-node q is not a decay operator or derived interacting species dynamics; a background-fit resemblance cannot identify microphysics.

This is the narrowly selected derivative/interpretation question within the reconstruction family, conditional on the named Union3 cubic-coordinate fit. It is not a general prediction of all interpolation cases.

The current source explicitly uses differing reduction/calibration pipelines and obtains compilation-dependent q constraints. The historical neighbour motivates a lineage audit; its older results do not demonstrate a specific bias in these current releases.
